IMPORTANT CAVEAT flagged by the task and independently verified: the citation as stated (case name 'People v. Anderson', year 1968, reporter '70 Cal.2d 15') IS a real, correctly-cited California Supreme Court opinion -- CourtListener's citation-search API returns exactly one match for '70 Cal.2d 15': People v. Anderson, date_filed 1968-12-23, parallel citations 447 P.2d 942 / 73 Cal.Rptr. 550, California Supreme Court. HOWEVER this is NOT the famous death-penalty/cruel-or-unusual-punishment case. That is a DIFFERENT case with the same name: People v. Anderson (1972) 6 Cal.3d 628, 493 P.2d 880 (which held the death penalty violated the CA Constitution's cruel-or-unusual-punishment clause; CourtListener opinion id 1260876). The 1968 case at 70 Cal.2d 15 instead concerns evidentiary standards for premeditation/deliberation in first-degree murder (the 'Anderson factors' -- planning activity, motive, and manner-of-killing evidence categories), arising from defendant Anderson's conviction for the 1962 murder of 10-year-old Victoria Hammond; he was sentenced to death and the case reached the Supreme Court on mandatory death-penalty review, but the holding is about premeditation proof, not death-penalty constitutionality. Wikipedia's own article on the 1968 case explicitly flags this ('Not to be confused with People v. Anderson (1972)'). So: citation text/case-name/reporter is CONFIRMED REAL and exact, but if the eval set's 'criminal / death penalty' topic tag was meant to signal the cruel-or-unusual-punishment holding, that holding belongs to the other Anderson case (6 Cal.3d 628), not to 70 Cal.2d 15. Could not obtain a clean verbatim excerpt of the 1968 opinion text itself from a reachable primary source: courts.ca.gov archive does not cover 1968 opinions (404), and both courtlistener.com and law.justia.com opinion pages returned blank/403 to WebFetch (likely bot-blocked or JS-rendered); only paraphrased snippets from CourtListener's search index and secondary summaries (Wikipedia, Quimbee, casemine) were obtainable.
